chunks: For him are angels in succession, before him and behind him, who protect him by God's command. Indeed, God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when God intends for a people misfortune, there is no repelling it, and no guardian will they have besides Him.

key_terms.مُعَقِّبَاتٌ: Angels in succession, following one another

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between human action and divine decree regarding protection and misfortune?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'Mu'aqibat' (successive angels) are often interpreted not only as general guardians but specifically as the angels of the Imams or the divine agents who preserve the community through the era of Occultation. This verse underscores the dynamic nature of divine decree, linking external circumstances to internal spiritual states, a concept central to the Shia understanding of how the Imams guide the faithful through periods of both prosperity and tribulation.
